name: Challenge
definition: We form a long-term vision, meeting challenges with courage and creativity to realize our dreams.

rows.under: Plans to the next review. The destination is whatever will be easy to hit.
rows.justRight: Names a destination years out, then picks the work that actually moves toward it.
rows.over: Announces a 20-year vision and cannot say what this week is for.

rows.under: Shrinks the goal until it fits the current method.
rows.justRight: Holds the goal and invents a path that has a chance of reaching it.
rows.over: Treats every constraint as optional, and the team spends a year on a path that was never going to work.

rows.under: Drops the goal. Failure is treated as proof it was the wrong dream.
rows.justRight: Keeps the destination and changes the method. Courage is staying with the problem, not with the first idea.
rows.over: Repeats the same try louder, because changing course would look like giving up.

rows.situation: When people say it cannot be done
rows.justRight: Asks what would have to be true, then tests the smallest version of that.
rows.over: Dismisses every objection as lack of courage, including the ones that would have saved the work.

rows.situation: When the next step has real risk
rows.under: Waits for a path with no downside. The vision stays a slide.
rows.justRight: Takes the risk that is required, with eyes open, and owns what happens.
rows.over: Picks the dramatic option so that people will see the courage.

rows.situation: When the known method will not reach the goal
rows.justRight: Changes the method. Creativity is in service of the destination, not a substitute for it.
rows.over: Collects novel ideas and never commits to one long enough to learn.
